question.text: A Professional Clearing Member (PCM) is entitled to:

answer.text: Clear and settle trades executed by other members and is not entitled to execute exchange trades except for risk-management purposes
Both trade and clear on their own account
Trade only on their own account
Only provide research and advisory services

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that a Professional Clearing Member clears and settles trades executed by Trading Members and Trading-cum-Clearing Members and is not entitled to execute trades on the exchange unless it is for risk-management purposes. The Trap: A PCM is not a general trading member. It does not trade on its own account in the normal course, nor does it provide research and advisory services as part of its PCM role. Note: The explanation keeps the source caveat that exchange trades by a PCM are restricted to risk-management purposes only.
